# ModScope
### A Python toolkit for downstream DNA methylation analysis from Oxford Nanopore sequencing data

[![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.8%2B-3776AB?style=flat-square&logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://www.python.org/)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green?style=flat-square)](LICENSE)

---

## Overview

**ModScope** is a modular command-line toolkit for the analysis of DNA base modification data generated by [Oxford Nanopore Technologies](https://nanoporetech.com/). Starting from the bedmethyl output of [ModKit](https://github.com/nanoporetech/modkit), the toolkit provides two independent but interoperable analysis modules:

- **Motif Discovery** — identifies the sequence context (motif) associated with DNA methylation using a genetic algorithm-based search with statistical validation
- **Methylome Profiler** — characterizes genome-wide methylation patterns at the gene, region, and nucleotide level

Designed for bacterial/prokaryotic genome analysis (e.g. restriction-modification system characterization), but adaptable to any organism with a reference genome and annotation.

---

## Pipeline Overview

```
Oxford Nanopore Reads
        │
        ▼
   [ModKit pileup]
        │
        └──── bedmethyl file (.bed / .tsv)
                    │
        ┌───────────┴────────────┐
        │                        │
        ▼                        ▼
 MOTIF DISCOVERY          METHYLOME PROFILER
 ─────────────────        ──────────────────
 Akmaker.py               mod_mapper.py
        │                        │
        ▼                        ├──► annotate_methylome.py
 motif_discovery_GA.py           │
        │                        └──► methylation_sliding_window.py
        ▼
   mod_calc.py
```

---

## Modules

### Module 1: Motif Discovery

Identifies the specific DNA sequence motifs that are targeted for methylation. Takes advantage of the k-mer context embedded in bedmethyl output to extract sequence windows around modified bases, then applies a genetic algorithm to search for enriched motifs.

#### Scripts

---

#### `Akmaker.py` — K-mer Extraction

Extracts k-mers of user-defined length centered on predicted modified bases from a bedmethyl file + reference genome. Supports extraction of:
- **Positive sequences** — k-mers at positions predicted as modified (above a user-defined modification frequency threshold)
- **Negative control sequences** — k-mers at positions predicted as unmodified
- **Random control sequences** — randomly sampled k-mers from the reference genome

Output is in FASTA format for downstream use in `motif_discovery_GA.py`.

**Usage:**
```bash
# Extract positive (methylated) k-mers
python Akmaker.py \
  -bed sample.bed \
  -ref genome.fasta \
  -modified \
  -len 31 \
  -depth 10 \
  -mod_threshold 70.0 \
  -mod_base A \
  -out sample_prefix

# Extract negative control k-mers
python Akmaker.py \
  -bed sample.bed \
  -ref genome.fasta \
  -negative \
  -neg_sample 1000 \
  -len 31 \
  -depth 10 \
  -mod_base A \
  -out sample_prefix
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-bed` | ModKit bedmethyl TSV file | required |
| `-ref` | Reference genome (FASTA/multi-FASTA) | required |
| `-modified` | Extract k-mers at modified positions | — |
| `-negative` | Extract k-mers at unmodified positions | — |
| `-all` | Extract k-mers at all positions meeting depth filter | — |
| `-len` | K-mer length (odd number recommended) | `31` |
| `-depth` | Minimum read depth to include a position | `10` |
| `-mod_threshold` | Minimum % of reads called modified to define a position as methylated | `70.0` |
| `-mod_base` | Modified base type (`A` or `C`) | `A` |
| `-neg_sample` | Number of negative control k-mers to sample | `1000` |
| `-out` | Output file prefix | required |

**Outputs:**
- `<prefix>_positive_seqs.fasta` — methylated k-mers
- `<prefix>_negative_seqs.fasta` — unmodified control k-mers
- `<prefix>_control_seqs.fasta` — random genomic control k-mers

---

#### `motif_discovery_GA.py` — Genetic Algorithm Motif Search

Searches for sequence motifs enriched in methylated k-mers relative to negative controls using a genetic algorithm. The algorithm initializes a population of random motifs of user-defined length and iteratively selects and mutates the best-scoring candidates (those with the highest positional conservation at non-modified positions) across multiple generations. All candidate motifs in the final population are evaluated using Fisher's exact test against the negative control sequences.

The modified base position is searched across all positions within the motif length, allowing unbiased identification of the true methylation site within the motif.

**Usage:**
```bash
python motif_discovery_GA.py \
  -m positive_seqs.fasta \
  -u negative_seqs.fasta \
  -k 6 \
  -b A \
  -g 100 \
  -n 100

# Mask a known dominant motif to search for secondary motifs
python motif_discovery_GA.py \
  -m positive_seqs.fasta \
  -u negative_seqs.fasta \
  -k 6 \
  -b A \
  --mask_motif GATC
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-m` / `--methylated` | Multi-FASTA of methylated k-mers (from `Akmaker.py`) | required |
| `-u` / `--unmethylated` | Multi-FASTA of negative control k-mers | required |
| `-k` / `--motif_length` | Length of motif to search for | required |
| `-b` / `--modified_base` | Base predicted to be modified (`A` or `C`) | `A` |
| `-g` / `--generations` | Number of evolutionary generations | `100` |
| `-n` / `--population` | Population size per generation | `100` |
| `--mask_motif` | Comma-separated list of motifs to exclude from search | — |

**Output** (stdout, tab-separated):
```
motif    mod_pos    p_value    odds_ratio    meth_hits    unmeth_hits
GATCAG   2          1.2e-45    18.34         842          12
...
```
Top 20 candidate motifs sorted by Fisher's exact test p-value.

---

#### `mod_calc.py` — Motif Methylation Frequency

Quantifies the fraction of a given motif's occurrences in the genome that are methylated. Accepts standard IUPAC ambiguity codes in motif definitions (e.g. `RGATCY`), automatically expanding to all valid sequence combinations. Returns per-motif counts, percent methylation, and genome-wide summary statistics.

**Usage:**
```bash
# Single motif
python mod_calc.py \
  -bed sample.bed \
  -ref genome.fasta \
  -motif GATC \
  -mod_pos 1 \
  -mod_base A \
  -mod_call_thresh 70.0 \
  -min_cov 10 \
  -out results_prefix

# From a file containing a list of motifs
python mod_calc.py \
  -bed sample.bed \
  -ref genome.fasta \
  -motif_file motif_list.txt \
  -mod_base A \
  -out results_prefix
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-bed` | ModKit bedmethyl TSV file | required |
| `-ref` | Reference genome (FASTA) | required |
| `-motif` | Single motif string (IUPAC codes accepted) | — |
| `-motif_file` | Text file with one motif per line | — |
| `-mod_base` | Modified base type | `A` |
| `-mod_pos` | Position of the modified base within the motif (0-indexed) | required |
| `-mod_call_thresh` | Modification frequency threshold for calling a position modified | `70.0` |
| `-min_cov` | Minimum read depth filter | `10` |
| `-out` | Output file prefix | — |

**Output:**
- Stdout: per-motif table of occurrences, modified count, and % methylated; genome-wide totals
- `<prefix>_mod_calc.tsv` (if `-out` specified)

---

### Module 2: Methylome Profiler

Characterizes genome-wide DNA methylation patterns at multiple scales: per-position, per-gene/feature, and across sliding genomic windows.

#### Scripts

---

#### `mod_mapper.py` — Modification Site Mapping

Maps ModKit bedmethyl calls to genomic coordinates in a standardized format compatible with all downstream scripts in the Methylome Profiler module. Optionally cross-references positions against a set of known methylation target motifs (e.g. restriction-modification recognition sequences), labeling each site as `modified`, `unmodified`, or `off_target`.

**Usage:**
```bash
# Basic mapping
python mod_mapper.py \
  -bed sample.bed \
  -ref genome.fasta \
  -motif GATC \
  -mod_pos 1 \
  -mod_call_thresh 70.0 \
  -min_cov 10

# From motif file, output only target modified sites
python mod_mapper.py \
  -bed sample.bed \
  -ref genome.fasta \
  -motif_file motifs_with_positions.txt \
  -target_mods_only
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-bed` | ModKit bedmethyl TSV file | required |
| `-ref` | Reference genome (FASTA) | required |
| `-motif` | Single target motif (IUPAC codes accepted) | — |
| `-motif_file` | TSV file: column 1 = motif, column 2 = mod position | — |
| `-mod_pos` | Position of modified base within motif (0-indexed) | required with `-motif` |
| `-mod_call_thresh` | Modification frequency threshold | `50.0` |
| `-min_cov` | Minimum read depth | `10` |
| `-target_mods_only` | Output only sites within target motifs predicted as modified | — |

**Output** (stdout, tab-separated):
```
motif    chromosome    position    strand    status
GATC     chr1          14523       +         modified
GATC     chr1          18901       -         unmodified
off_target  chr1       22104       +         modified
```

---

#### `annotate_methylome.py` — Gene-level Methylation Annotation

Parses a GenBank flat file (`.gbff`) to build a complete map of all coding sequences and intergenic regions in the genome, then tallies methylation counts (target modified, target unmodified, and off-target modified) within each genomic feature. Reports methylation rates normalized per kilobase (mods/kb) to allow comparison across features of varying length.

Takes output from `mod_mapper.py` as the methylation site input.

**Usage:**
```bash
python annotate_methylome.py \
  -gbff genome_annotation.gbff \
  -sites mod_mapper_output.tsv \
  -out annotation_prefix
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `-gbff` | GenBank flat file annotation (must match reference genome) |
| `-sites` | Tab-separated mod sites file (output from `mod_mapper.py`) |
| `-out` | Output file prefix |

**Outputs:**
- `<prefix>_mod_annotations.tsv` — per-feature table with modification counts and rates for all CDS and intergenic regions
- `<prefix>_annotated_sites.tsv` — per-site table with gene annotation for each methylation call
- `<prefix>_mod_summary.tsv` — per-replicon summary: total, CDS, intergenic, and off-target methylation counts and rates

**Output columns (`_mod_annotations.tsv`):**

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `element_id` | Chromosome / plasmid identifier |
| `gene_id` | Locus tag or `intergenic` |
| `protein_id` | Protein accession (if available) |
| `start` / `end` | Feature coordinates |
| `feature_len` | Feature length (bp) |
| `target_mod` | Count of methylated target motif sites |
| `mod_rate` | Methylation density (mods per kb) |
| `target_no_mod` | Count of unmodified target motif sites |
| `off_target` | Count of off-target methylation events |

---

#### `methylation_sliding_window.py` — Sliding Window Analysis

Applies a sliding window across each genomic element to compute the density of methylated sites within each window, enabling identification of methylation hotspots and regional clustering patterns. Takes output from `mod_mapper.py` as input.

**Usage:**
```bash
python methylation_sliding_window.py \
  -sites mod_mapper_output.tsv \
  -seq_len seq_lengths.tsv \
  -win 5000 \
  -step 500 \
  -out sliding_window_prefix

# Include off-target methylation events in window counts
python methylation_sliding_window.py \
  -sites mod_mapper_output.tsv \
  -seq_len seq_lengths.tsv \
  -win 5000 \
  -step 500 \
  -all \
  -out sliding_window_prefix
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-sites` | Mod sites file from `mod_mapper.py` | required |
| `-seq_len` | TSV file with columns `id` and `len` (sequence lengths) | required |
| `-win` | Window size (bp) | required |
| `-step` | Step size (bp) | required |
| `-all` | Include off-target methylation in window counts | — |
| `-out` | Output file prefix (prints to stdout if omitted) | — |

**Output** (`<prefix>_windows.tsv`):

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `id` | Sequence / replicon identifier |
| `start` | Window start coordinate |
| `end` | Window end coordinate |
| `mods` | Number of methylated sites in window |

## Dependencies

| Package | Version | Usage |
|---|---|---|
| `biopython` | ≥ 1.79 | Sequence I/O, k-mer extraction |
| `pandas` | ≥ 1.3 | Tabular data manipulation |
| `numpy` | ≥ 1.21 | Numerical operations |
| `scipy` | ≥ 1.7 | Fisher's exact test, binomial testing |

Install dependencies via pip:
```bash
pip install biopython pandas numpy scipy
```

This toolkit also depends on internal utility modules (`tools_and_utilities/seq_tools` and `tools_and_utilities/mod_tools`) included in this repository.

---

## Input File Requirements

### ModKit bedmethyl (`.bed`)
Standard output from `modkit pileup`. Expected column format (0-indexed):

| Col | Field | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | chromosome | Sequence/contig name |
| 1 | start | 0-based position |
| 2 | end | End position |
| 3 | mod | Modification type (e.g. `a`, `m`) |
| 4 | score | Score |
| 5 | strand | `+` or `-` |
| 9 | cov | Read depth |
| 10 | mod_freq | Fraction of reads called modified |
| 11–17 | counts | N_mod, N_can, N_other, N_del, N_fail, N_diff, N_nocall |

### Reference Genome (`.fasta`)
Standard single or multi-FASTA. Sequence IDs must match the `chromosome` column in the bedmethyl file.

### GenBank Annotation (`.gbff`)
Standard GenBank flat file format. The sequence identifiers must match the reference genome used for read mapping.

---

## Recommended Workflow

```
1.  Run Oxford Nanopore basecalling with modification detection enabled
        └── (e.g. Dorado with 6mA or 5mC model)

2.  Generate bedmethyl pileup with ModKit
        └── modkit pileup aligned.bam output.bed --ref genome.fasta

3.  [Motif Discovery]
    a.  Akmaker.py       → extract positive and negative k-mers (FASTA)
    b.  motif_discovery_GA.py  → identify enriched methylation motifs
    c.  mod_calc.py      → quantify genome-wide methylation of discovered motifs

4.  [Methylome Profiler]
    a.  mod_mapper.py    → map and label modification sites
    b.  annotate_methylome.py  → per-gene and per-region methylation tallies
    c.  methylation_sliding_window.py  → hotspot and regional distribution analysis
```
